items.Title: Hiring Event - Part Time Associate Banker Santa Clarita  West (30 Hours)
items.ExternalDescriptionStr:
At Chase, we are passionate about creating memorable experiences for our clients and employees, making them feel welcomed, valued, and understood. We build lasting relationships by doing the right thing, exceeding expectations, and embracing diversity and inclusion. 

As an Associate Banker within Chase, you will represent our brand and culture with the utmost hospitality, using the latest banking solutions and cutting-edge financial technology combined with friendly and attentive service.  Your role at Chase will significantly contribute to the branch's success by delivering exceptional client experiences. You will build trusted relationships with clients, sharing product knowledge and solutions – helping clients achieve their financial goals. 

Job Responsibilities 
  • Create a welcoming environment by delivering attentive and friendly service by greeting clients as they enter the branch, making them feel heard and cared for, leveraging a tablet to manage lobby traffic, check clients into the waiting queue, and schedule/cancel client meetings.
  • Exceed client expectations by providing account servicing and maintenance as well as opening new accounts, while complying with all policies, procedures, and regulatory and banking requirements.
  • Educate and assist clients with day-to-day banking transactions including the usage of technology self-service options such as leveraging the Chase Mobile App, Chase.com, and ATMs can help them with their banking needs whenever, wherever, and however they want.
  • Build meaningful relationships with clients by actively listening, asking thoughtful questions, demonstrating empathy, and sharing product knowledge and solutions – partnering with other branch team members to help achieve their financial goals.
  • Perform branch operations, which may include managing cash devices such as the cash vault, ATM, or others while adhering to all bank policies and procedures.
Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills
  • Ability to put clients first and exceed their expectations – delivering attentive and friendly service, creating a welcoming environment. 
  • Ability to build trusted relationships – demonstrating genuine care and concern during interactions with clients.
  • Ability to engage clients – communicating clearly and politely to understand and help, anticipating client needs.
  • Ability to quickly and effectively resolve client issues with attention to detail – providing a consistent client experience.  
  • Ability to elevate the client experience – working collaboratively as a team to deliver seamless service with care and sincerity.
  • Ability to quickly and accurately learn products, services, and procedures.
  • Client service experience or comparable experience.
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent.
Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills
  • Strong desire and ability to influence, educate, and connect customers to technology solutions.
  • Cash handling experience.

FEDERAL DEPOSIT INSURANCE ACT:

This position is subject to Section 19 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act. As such, an employment offer for this position is contingent on JPMorganChase’s review of criminal conviction history, including pretrial diversions or program entries.

items.Title: Liquidity Controller Analyst
items.ExternalDescriptionStr:
Help shape how we manage liquidity and balance sheet priorities for a global financial institution. In this role, you’ll turn complex data and market activity into clear reporting and actionable insights. You’ll partner closely across finance and treasury to strengthen controls, transparency, and decision-making. If you enjoy solving problems, improving processes, and working in a fast-paced environment, you’ll find meaningful impact here.

Job summary

As a Liquidity Controller Analyst in Commercial and Investment Bank Treasury, you support daily liquidity reporting, analysis, and controls that help us manage liquidity, balance sheet, and capital priorities. You’ll work with partners across treasury and product control to ensure results are accurate, explainable, and delivered on time. You’ll contribute to regulatory and management initiatives by producing clear metrics, reconciliations, and presentations. You’ll also help us execute process improvements that make our funding, liquidity, and capital reporting more efficient and resilient.

Job responsibilities

  • Oversee daily liquidity-related financial reporting, including detailed reconciliations, review, and presentations
  • Prepare and validate key liquidity metrics and supporting analyses for management and stakeholders
  • Apply working knowledge of financial products (for example, deposits, commitments, derivatives, and secured funding) in reporting and analysis
  • Interpret and apply applicable liquidity and capital guidance in day-to-day analysis and reporting activities
  • Partner with product control and corporate treasury teams to confirm results and resolve breaks
  • Investigate data variances, identify root causes, and document conclusions and remediation steps
  • Build clear narratives and materials that communicate results, drivers, and risks to stakeholders
  • Lead timely execution of assigned deliverables while balancing multiple priorities and deadlines
  • Execute ad hoc analyses and projects for senior management and regulatory initiatives
  • Improve and streamline processes through optimization and rationalization efforts across funding, liquidity, and capital

 

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field
  • 1 year of experience in accounting, finance, or a related field
  • Demonstrated ability to perform detailed reconciliations and data quality checks with strong attention to detail
  • Ability to analyze large datasets and summarize findings into clear takeaways
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create concise presentations
  • Proven organizational skills and ability to manage multiple deliverables in a deadline-driven environment
  • Ability to work with limited supervision and take ownership of assigned tasks through completion
  • Demonstrated problem-solving skills, including ability to investigate variances and identify root causes

 

Preferred qualifications, capabilities and skills

  • Familiarity with capital and liquidity risk regulations
  • Experience partnering with treasury, product control, or related finance teams
  • Familiarity with internal finance or reporting systems
  • Experience using Python for data analysis or automation
  • Experience using Tableau for reporting and visualization
  • Experience working with Snowflake or similar data platforms
  • Experience using Alteryx or similar workflow tools

 

Additional Information

To be eligible for this role, you must be authorized to work in the United States. We do not offer any type of employment-based immigration sponsorship for this role. Likewise, JPMorgan Chase & Co. will not provide any assistance or sign any documentation in support of any other form of immigration sponsorship or benefit, including optional practical training (OPT) or curricular practical training (CPT).

payload.ShortDescriptionStr: Drive innovation and solution delivery while leading a technical area and serving as a primary decision maker for your teams

items.Title: Director of Software Engineering — Securities Lending Technology
items.ExternalDescriptionStr:
The Securities Lending technology organisation within J.P. Morgan's Commercial & Investment Bank builds and operates the Enterprise Finance Platform (EFP) — the firm's strategic, end-to-end system of record for securities lending and equity finance globally. EFP processes billions of dollars of transactions daily across equities, fixed income, and repo products, serving institutional clients and internal trading desks across APAC, EMEA, and NA. The platform spans the full securities lending lifecycle: pre-trade locate and availability, rate management, trading, trade entry and lifecycle management, post-trade settlement, and reconciliation. The APAC engineering hub in Hong Kong is the primary technology presence covering Asian market hours and is a critical node in the firm's global follow-the-sun engineering model.

As a Director of Software Engineering at JPMorganChase within the Securities Lending technology, you lead a technical area and drive impact within teams, technologies, and projects across departments. Utilize your in-depth knowledge of software, applications, technical processes, and product management to drive multiple complex projects and initiatives, while serving as a primary decision maker for your teams and be a driver of innovation and solution delivery. 

Job responsibilities

  • Lead, develop, and retain a team of engineers and technical programme managers in Hong Kong, covering the Pre-Trade and GRIPS platform domains
  • Own the APAC engineering delivery roadmap, balancing business demand, regulatory requirements, and technical modernisation priorities
  • Serve as the senior technical stakeholder for the APAC trading desk and business partners, providing engineering insight and risk assessment for platform changes affecting Asian market hours
  • Drive technical excellence across the team — code quality, test discipline, reliability, and continuous improvement of engineering practices
  • Represent APAC engineering in cross-domain programme forums including EU T+1, the Morfin Pre-Trade modernisation programme, and quarterly planning cycles
  • Partner with product and business to translate strategic priorities into engineering deliverables, and with peer EDs globally to ensure consistent platform governance
  • Build the APAC engineering capability over the medium term, including headcount planning, graduate hiring (SEP), and succession development
  • Champion AI-assisted engineering adoption — the organisation has one of the highest AI tool usage rates in the firm and expects engineering leaders to model and  accelerate that adoption
Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills
  • Proven engineering leadership at Director / Executive Director level, with experience managing teams of 10+ engineers in a financial services or similarly complex, regulated environment
  • Deep technical background in Java-based distributed systems, event-driven architecture (Kafka/MSK), and cloud-native deployment (AWS, Kubernetes)
  • Experience leading engineering in a trading, capital markets, or financial technology environment — familiarity with securities lending, equity finance, or prime brokerage is a strong advantage
  • Track record of developing senior engineering talent through promotion and recognition pipelines
  • Ability to operate in a globally matrixed organisation, influencing without direct authority across EMEA and NA engineering counterparts
  • Clear communicator — able to articulate technical risk and delivery status to both engineering peers and non-technical business stakeholders
  • Experience with modern engineering excellence practices: CI/CD, SonarQube quality gates, PR review discipline, and engineering scorecards
  • Genuine interest in AI tooling and its application to developer productivity — the team uses Copilot and Claude Code extensively and leadership is expected to set the standard
